title: Mastery of Filamentary Keratitis (FK)
summary: Filamentary Keratitis is a chronic, often recalcitrant ocular surface disorder characterized by the presence of mobile, mucus-rich filaments attached to the corneal epithelium. It represents a hallmark sign of underlying tear film instability and severe dry eye disease.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: FK is defined by the formation of strands (filaments) composed of degenerated epithelial cells and mucus, anchored to the corneal basement membrane. Pathophysiology: The inciting factor is usually a localized epithelial defect or chronic ocular surface irritation. The 'three-hit hypothesis' involves 1) Decreased tear production/mucin deficiency, 2) Epithelial basement membrane instability, and 3) Excessive eyelid movement (mechanical tugging) causing the mucus to coalesce into a stalk.

sections.title: Clinical Presentation & Symptoms
content: Foreign body sensation (often severe)
Photophobia and reflex lacrimation
Blepharospasm
Fluctuating visual acuity due to filament movement
Mucoid discharge
Intense ocular burning/pain

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup (Process)
content: Step 1: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy (white light).
Step 2: Instill Fluorescein/Rose Bengal/Lissamine Green.
Step 3: Identify comma-shaped filaments staining brightly.
Step 4: Assess tear break-up time (TBUT) and Schirmer I/II.
Step 5: Evert lids to rule out concretions or SLK.

rows: History of trauma, often no filaments

sections.title: Management Algorithm
content: 1. Immediate: Mechanical removal of filaments using fine jewelers forceps.
2. Topical: Preservative-free artificial tears (qid to hourly).
3. Mucolytic: N-acetylcysteine 5-10% drops (dissolves mucus).
4. Stabilization: Punctal occlusion (plugs) to increase reservoir.
5. Anti-inflammatory: Topical cyclosporine 0.05% or Lifitegrast.
6. Severe: Bandage contact lens (extended wear) or autologous serum.

sections.title: Red Flags (Emergency Signs)
content: Ulceration at base of filament (Infectious keratitis risk)
Melting of the underlying stroma
Severe thinning or impending perforation
Associated hypopyon

content.explanation: M-Mucolytic (N-acetylcysteine), U-Underlying (Dry eye workup), C-Cleaning (Manual removal), U-Uncover (SLK/Toxicity), S-Stabilization (Punctal plugs/Serum).

sections.title: Recent Advances
content: Recent focus on 'Ocular Surface Microbiome' in patients with persistent filaments.
Utilization of Amniotic Membrane Transplantation (AMT) for recalcitrant cases to promote epithelial healing.
Emerging data on Scleral Lenses (e.g., PROSE treatment) as the gold standard for severe underlying neurotrophic/dry eye states.
